newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian shares end touch firmer but well off highs.
newsitem.headline: Italian shares end touch firmer but well off highs.

text.p: Italian stocks ran out of steam in late business on Thursday and closed with only modest gains after coming off session highs in fairly thin and directionless trade.
Traders saw no real reason for the settling back given Wall Street's firmness and comments from Fed Chairman Alan Greenspan which were seen as mildy bullish.
"The market is consolidating positions with more selective buying and perhaps funds prefer to put a brake on prices for the moment," one dealer said.
The all-share Mibtel index closed up 0.39 percent at 12,246 after a 12,231-12,354 range and the Mib30 blue chip index ended up 0.44 percent at 18,220 after an 18,190-18,411 range.

Hi-tech group Olivetti ended 5.22 percent lower at 617 lire and was the most traded stock with over 76 million shares changing hands. Olivetti announced preliminary 1996 results on Wednesday, showing a pre-tax loss of around 800 billion lire with sales down 16 percent.
Former Olivetti chairman Carlo De Benedetti's industrial holding CIR gained 2.34 percent to 1,183 lire against the trend, but his Cofide financial holding lost 1.36 percent to 740.

Fiat closed 1.51 percent off at 5,145 lire ahead of 1996 results after the market closed. Fiat said its 1996 operating profit fell to some 1.8 trillion lire after 1995's 3.325 trillion while sales rose three percent to some 78 trillion.
Also after the market closed, CIR said it had sold shares in Olivetti on the market bringing its current stake down to 9.3 percent. Its stake at end-1996 stood at 12.8 percent.

Telecoms were mixed ahead of board meetings expected later today of Stet holding and Telecom Italia to approve the fusion plan announced by the Treasury on January 24 as a prelude to Stet's planned privatisation. Stet was 0.71 percent up at 7,754 lire and Telecom Italia put on 0.38 percent to 4,516 but mobile phone operator TIM shed 0.87 percent to 4,694.
Provisional stock market data put total traded value at 1.13 trillion lire, down on the previous session's 1.22 trillion.
